synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Eliana Lin and Wang Yu Chen grew up next door to each other in the Walled City, with a knee-high wall between their front steps. On the night she finishes school she can't sleep and goes to sit on her step at two in the morning. He comes out with his blanket and sits down beside her, and somewhere before dawn he realises he's in love with her. In the morning he turns down the better medical school in the north and follows her up the hill. He tells everyone it was the course.

She works it out in a fortnight and climbs onto his roof at Mid-Autumn to tell him to stop hovering. He kisses her before she's finished the sentence. After that they're together, in secret, because that's how she wants it. She's the youngest Lin, born the night her mother died, and her father can barely look at her. At night, on five screens, she cleans the family's name out of places it shouldn't be, for Chen Si, and tells nobody. Yu Chen never asks her to stop. He brings tea.

Nobody cheats, and nothing hangs on a misunderstanding. The hard parts are being seen (holding his hand on the hill in daylight), a father who has never once asked her what she wants, and one word she has been afraid of all her life, because people say forever and then they're in a hospital. He's willing to wait, and he won't pretend he isn't.

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Eliana has been in the corner of every Lin book so far: asleep under a ladder, filming everyone's kisses for the spreadsheet, opening Haozhen's phone in under four minutes. I kept wondering who was waiting for her on the kerb when she got home.

Yu Chen looks like the clean one, and mostly he is. But he reads her food orders every night because they're on his card, he picked his medical school because of her, and he lied once, to his face, to the cousin who raised him. I didn't want the book to tell him off for any of that. What I love most about him is that in seven years he never once asks her to be someone else. He makes more tea.

This is the softest book I've written since The Softest Kind of Love. They're adults the whole way through and they get together early. Their first times are shy and clumsy, with a lot of laughing and starting again, because he researches everything and she wrecks the plan. Her father is hard on her, and there's a death in an emergency department and a bad morning at the flower market. Nobody has a baby. They get a porch, a jar in a wall and two desks facing each other.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a 21+ friends-to-lovers romance, gentle and funny for most of its length, but it has some hard moments:

• Love scenes throughout, heated and detailed but not explicit, from He Researched This Part Too on

• A mother who died giving birth, mentioned, and a father's grief and coldness towards the daughter she had (throughout; most of all Nineteen, and Nobody Says It, The Neighbour and the Cold Gaze, The First Lin Child to Say No to His Face and Elowen Takes Her Side)

• The heroine's secret work for a crime syndicate, and a man's hands broken because of something she found, mentioned (He Already Knew)

• A sister abducted, and human trafficking referred to but not shown (The Fence, The Photograph)

• A nineteen-year-old's death after a road accident, with resuscitation in an emergency department (The Night He Lost One)

• Threatening messages and photographs from strangers (The Boy Next Door, He Always Waits)

• A cyber-attack on the family, a crowd stampede, a crushed leg and heavy bleeding (The Breach, Thirty-Six Hours, Someone Else's Blood)

• An attack with a broken bottle at work, a head injury and stitches (The Ring in the Jar)

• A partner who reads her food orders to know when she hasn't eaten, and a lie told to the police for her, shown without judgement (He Already Knew, The Detective Already Knows)

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
Yu-er — Eliana's family name. Her sisters use it when they want something. Yu Chen uses it all the time, and it's the only time it comes without a favour attached.
The tall house — the Lin family house in the Walled City: old, narrow, too many stairs, a red door, and three front steps under a small tiled roof.
The porch — those three steps, with the crack in the third one, where everything that matters between them happens at two in the morning. From 2026 it runs the width of both houses.
The old Song house — next door to the Lins. Yu Chen's uncle's house, which he bought from Wei Long; later rebuilt with one long room and two desks facing each other.
The persimmon tree — in the Song garden. Its best branch hangs over the Lin side, so by old neighbourly rule its fruit are Lin persimmons. Ripe every October.
The jar — a plum-jam jar of Nainai's, kept behind a loose brick in the garden wall under the persimmon branch. Notes go in it. You don't read one until the writer has gone inside.
The Eraser — what the Syndicate calls Eliana, because she erases the Lin family's footprints. She hates the name.
The fence — what she built in October 2022, after her sister was taken: a watch on the family's names, faces and addresses that wakes her wherever she is. Two short buzzes mean family.
FENCE — her own security firm, from March 2026, in two rooms above a dumpling shop on Terrace Road. For the first month the sign was a sticky note: FENCE. Legal. Mostly.
The Spreadsheet — Eliana's record of every family secret, kept for years. "You're on a spreadsheet" is a warning.
DRAW (OFFICIAL) — Eliana's caption on the video of the paper twins' birthday party at Fig Tree Lane. Raiden contests it every year.
Red egg — a boiled egg dyed red, a traditional birthday gift. One is left at Eliana's door before dawn every 18 February. She thinks for years she knows who leaves it.
Study room 4B — the quiet room at the end of the library's fourth floor, booked to "Wang Y.C." every weekday morning since March 2022. Nobody has ever found out how.
Graduate-entry medicine — a four-year medical degree for students who already have a first degree. Yu Chen's, at the university on the hill, 2021 to 2025.
OSCE — the practical part of medical finals: timed stations with examiners and actors playing patients.
Mid-Autumn — the harvest festival at the full moon of the eighth lunar month: mooncakes, family dinners and lanterns. Every year Yu Chen puts a white rabbit lantern on his roof.
PLAN — Yu Chen's plans, in capitals, on small squares of paper. PLAN, PLAN B, PLAN C. She wrecks every one.
Nainai — grandmother on the father's side. Yu Chen's lives in the north and has had a letter from him every month for years.
The Lins, the Wangs and the Songs — Yu Chen's father was a Wang from the north, the younger brother of Xing Yue's father. His mother was a Song, Wei Long's aunt, which is how he came to live in the old Song house next door to the Lins.

chapters.title: The Boy Next Door Who Never Left
chapters.desc: The night she finishes school, Eliana can’t sleep and goes to sit on her front step at two in the morning. Yu Chen brings his blanket out and sits with her, and before it gets light he works out that he’s in love with her.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to talk. I’ll just sit here. That’s allowed.” — Wang Yu Chen

chapters.title: Two Gowns, Eventually
chapters.desc: First day on the hill. Eliana starts computer science and would like to be invisible, and Yu Chen has somehow started medicine at the same university and swears it’s about the course.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s the best medical course in the country. You being here is a coincidence.” — Wang Yu Chen

chapters.title: The Flask, the Headphones, the Tea
chapters.desc: Ten days in, Yu Chen has her new timetable memorised and a box of the headphones she destroys every fortnight. Eliana has found out she can’t concentrate when he turns pages, which is new and annoying.
chapters.epigraph: “I bought ten pairs. Don’t argue. You go through them like socks.” — Wang Yu Chen

chapters.title: Mid-Autumn, on the Roof
chapters.desc: Eliana climbs onto his roof at Mid-Autumn to pick a fight, because she’s worked out he didn’t end up at her university by accident. He doesn’t deny it. He kisses her in the middle of her sentence instead.
chapters.epigraph: “Stop. You’ve been circling me since September. I’m not blind. Say it.” — Eliana Lin

chapters.title: Not Official, She Says
chapters.desc: The morning after the roof, Eliana turns up with a typed list of rules: nobody knows, and it doesn’t get a name. Yu Chen agrees to every one of them and adds one of his own.
chapters.epigraph: “Fine. No name. But I’m not going to lie and say it isn’t the best thing that’s ever happened to me.” — Wang Yu Chen

chapters.title: The Drawing in His Pharmacology Notes
chapters.desc: Eliana can say anything with a keyboard and nothing out loud, so she hides a drawing in his notes and tells him not to look until he’s in the library. He looks in the library and has to walk out into the rain.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t look at it till you’re in the library. If you look on the bus I’ll know, because you go red on buses.” — Eliana Lin

chapters.title: He Researched This Part Too
chapters.desc: Their first night together goes nothing like his plan: it’s clumsy and shy, they keep laughing, and they start over twice. Afterwards, in the dark, he says the thing she’s most scared of so that she doesn’t have to.
chapters.epigraph: “I love you. You don’t have to say it back. I just didn’t want to be the only one who knew.” — Wang Yu Chen

chapters.title: He Already Knew
chapters.desc: After a bad job, Eliana finally tells him what she does at night, and finds out he’s known the outline since the summer: the nights she doesn’t eat, the light still on at four. She’s furious, and then she isn’t. He never once asks her to stop.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not going to ask you to stop. I’m going to keep feeding you. That’s all.” — Wang Yu Chen

chapters.title: The Second Winter
chapters.desc: The heating in the tall house breaks, and Eliana is sent to Zhao’s for the weekend after her father turns down Yu Chen’s offer of a warm room next door. They get through the weekend by text, and on Sunday night they meet at the garden wall.
chapters.epigraph: “He said no to my house. He didn’t say anything about the wall.” — Wang Yu Chen

chapters.title: Nineteen, and Nobody Says It
chapters.desc: On her birthday her father takes the family to the grave at dawn and won’t look at her, and there’s a red egg at her door like every year. That night Yu Chen gives her a whole sky to herself.
chapters.epigraph: “They wouldn’t let me bring a cake in. I asked. So you’ve got the ceiling instead.” — Wang Yu Chen

chapters.title: She Breaks a System for Fun
chapters.desc: Someone has been inside the wall Eliana built for Chen Si, fixed the one mistake she didn’t know she’d made, and sent him a bill for it. Eliana has never been beaten before. She takes it badly, so Yu Chen turns it into a dare.
chapters.epigraph: “She fixed my mistake and sent a bill. A bill. One day I’m going to beat her.” — Eliana Lin

chapters.title: Yu Chen Asks Raiden for Advice
chapters.desc: At Raiden and Evangeline’s birthday lunch, Yu Chen asks Raiden how to get on Lin Jian’s good side. The advice is useless, Eliana overhears it, and by the end both men are sworn to silence by a girl with a spreadsheet.
chapters.epigraph: “You want to date my sister. I want to go on living. I think we can help each other.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: A Hackathon, Allegedly
chapters.desc: He takes her to his family’s house by the sea for a weekend, and everyone at home thinks it’s a coding retreat. Wei Long, who raised him, rings twice with terrible advice. Nobody does any coding.
chapters.epigraph: “Bring fruit. Don’t talk about her father. Actually, don’t talk at all — you talk too much when you’re nervous.” — Song Wei Long

chapters.title: The Fence
chapters.desc: Evangeline disappears from the flower market and comes back changed, and Eliana, who can find anyone, couldn’t find her in time. Afterwards she builds something to watch for the Lin name, and won’t tell even Yu Chen what it’s for.
chapters.epigraph: “I was three days too slow. It won’t happen again. That’s all I can tell you.” — Eliana Lin

chapters.title: The Detective Already Knows
chapters.desc: Wei Long has worked out that the person the Syndicate calls “the Eraser” is the girl next door, the one the boy he raised is seeing. He comes to the garden wall off the record, to decide what to do about her, and to ask Yu Chen about a lie.
chapters.epigraph: “I asked you to your face. You looked at me and you lied. I raised you better than that. Or exactly that well.” — Song Wei Long

chapters.title: He Held the Ladder
chapters.desc: For Elowen’s flower-shop wedding, Eliana strings a sky of lights and won’t say why. The night before, a lanky boy holds her ladder for hours and slips out before anyone finds her asleep. At the wedding Raiden says “my wife” out loud, and nobody introduces the boy next door to anyone.
chapters.epigraph: “I’ll hold it. You do the stars. Don’t look down — you never look down.” — Wang Yu Chen

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.desc: At nineteen minutes past three in the morning, the fence catches the one thing it was built to catch. By ten she’s home and hollowed out, and the boy next door is on the kerb with his bicycle, because he always is.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to be scared on your own. That part’s mine. You can give me that part.” — Wang Yu Chen

chapters.title: The Night He Lost One
chapters.desc: On a Friday night in the emergency department, Yu Chen does chest compressions on a nineteen-year-old delivery rider, and nothing works. At two in the morning Eliana finds him on the east stairwell, and she stays until the sun comes up.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t have to say the right thing. You just don’t leave. I learned that from you.” — Eliana Lin

chapters.title: The Criminal Mind
chapters.desc: Eliana goes to a seminar to understand the men she hunts at night, and comes out with friends: a psychology student who never stops talking, her two sisters, and a cold profiler who looks at her half a second too long. Outside, Yu Chen breaks one of her rules.
chapters.epigraph: “I went to learn about monsters. I came home with a group chat.” — Eliana Lin

chapters.title: The Boy Next Door, He Always Waits
chapters.desc: A bank wants Eliana quiet, so her family sends Serafina’s fiancé to drive her to her own talk. Nobody tells Yu Chen anything. He’s on the kerb by half past five anyway, and at two in the morning he stops pretending there’s no name for what they are.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody. The boy next door. He always waits.” — Eliana Lin

descs.en: He thinks her hands are broken and opens every door for her. She secretly got her surgeon’s hands back, and works nights in a basement as the family’s ghost surgeon.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Elara Lin is a final-year medical student who talks all the time, practises stitches on bananas, and on her first morning on the surgical ward tells the chief resident he's missed a leak. She's right. By the end of the day Wang Xing Yue has handed her logbook to someone else, so that he can ask her to dinner. He's been in love with her for fifteen months. The only person he's told is his brother, who sent him a paper about voles.

She's also the Lins' surgeon. When the family's people bleed somewhere a hospital can't see them, she goes, with whatever she can steal. In a supply room at three in the morning she begs him not to ask, and he promises he won't. He keeps that promise for three and a half years: through a knife at her father's door that cuts through her right wrist, a winter when she stops talking, and the year she gets her hands back in secret on a machine in a garage and goes back to work in a cellar, in a mask, as Doctor Ghost.

He's known since she mended his pillowcase at two in the morning. He never asks her to stop. He restocks her bag instead, and when she finally calls him, he comes with blood.

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Elara has been in the corner of every Lin book so far: late, in scrubs, with her hair falling out of its clip, crying at weddings, stapling somebody's head on a kitchen table. I wanted to know what all that cost her, and who looks after the person who looks after everyone.

Xing Yue isn't a nice man to anyone but her. He makes residents sick on his ward rounds, he checks her location, he goes through her bag, and he lies to his own professor without blinking. I didn't want the book to tell him off for any of it. The one thing he never does is ask her to be someone else, and that felt like the most romantic thing I could give her.

There's blood, because it's a book about surgeons, but the medicine stays at story level. The love scenes are slow and mostly come after night shifts, in early light, which is how she likes them. Nobody has a baby. They get a house with a long kitchen, two pagers, a phone in a drawer that rings at half past eleven, and each other.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a 21+ medical romance, warm and funny for most of its length, but it has some hard moments:

• Love scenes throughout, heated and detailed but not explicit, from She Narrates Everything on

• An infected knife wound treated over the phone at night (Three in the Morning, on Speaker)

• A gunshot wound, sepsis and surgery on a kitchen table, with stolen hospital supplies (Zhao Zhendong Is Bleeding Out, Fifteen Days of Drips)

• A shooting in a noodle shop and a head wound closed at home (Staples on a Kitchen Table)

• A people-smuggling boat and cold, frightened survivors at a border bridge (The Seventh Guest)

• Burns after a workshop fire (Again?)

• A knife attack, heavy bleeding and a serious hand injury (The Knife at the Red Door)

• Nerve pain, withdrawal into silence, and a father's confession to a crime that killed her birth parents in a fire (The House Is Too Quiet, A Name in a Ledger, Elara Before the Lins)

• A prison visit (Her Mother's Window)

• Secret surgery outside hospitals, falsified records and lies to police and employers (A Surgeon Who Doesn't Exist, The Cellar Under the Rope Store, Doctor Ghost)

• A girl's face cut with a bottle by her father, mentioned (The Cellar Under the Rope Store)

• A gunshot to the thigh and life-threatening bleeding (Two Surgeons, One Table)

• A workplace inquiry and suspension (I Know)

• A footbridge collapse with many casualties (A Mass Casualty Night)

• A partner who tracks her phone and goes through her bag, shown without judgement (from Three in the Morning, on Speaker)

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
City Hospital — the teaching hospital at the foot of the hill. Ward 9B, general surgery, is on the ninth floor of the tower; the old 1930s block stands behind it.
Harbourside General — the big hospital by the harbour, where Elara does her intern year and goes back to training in 2027.
The Crestview — the private hospital on the hill above the old racecourse, where Dr. Meng repairs her hand and Ms. Cui makes her cry.
The hospital garden — behind the old block: a camphor tree older than the hospital, a koi pond, and the fourth window along on the first floor, which was her mother's ward.
14 Banyan Terrace — his flat, the top two floors and roof of a white 1950s building ten minutes downhill from City Hospital.
2 Camphor Hill — the old doctor's house above the hospital, with a long kitchen and a back room for the rig. Bought in both their names, without asking.
The Walled City — the old district where the Lins live, behind a red door with a brass fish knocker and eleven chairs that don't match.
The cellar under the rope store — the room Raiden builds next to the garage near the Docks, behind a steel door painted to look like wood.
Doctor Ghost — the name the docks give the masked surgeon who never speaks and always hums.
The rig — Jinx's steel training machine for Elara's hand: springs, a pinch gauge, pins and a wire that buzzes. Every knob turns a quarter.
The ghost phone — the line that rings only from her father's or Uncle Mok's numbers. From July 2027 it lives in the kitchen drawer.
The dot — her phone location, shared with him ‘for night shifts’ from 2023, and his with her from 2026.
The rules — what they wrote on the back of his suspension letter. Rule one: nobody does this alone.
Qu Xiaoyue — her birth name, ‘little moon’. Elara is a moon of Jupiter, so she kept a piece of it.
Qu Lighterage — her father's firm: four lighter boats between the ships and the old Walled City piers.
Plum Steps — the children's home at the top of a long flight of stone steps, closed in 2011.
Loupes — magnifying glasses surgeons wear to operate. Hers are dark red, made for her eyes, with E.L. inside the arm.
Registrar, consultant — a registrar is a mid-level surgeon in training; a consultant is the senior surgeon in charge.

chapters.title: The Student Who Told the Chief Resident He Was Wrong
chapters.desc: On her first morning in surgery, a final-year student tells the chief resident he’s missed a leak. She’s right, and he has seen her face before.
chapters.epigraph: “I’d rather be wrong about this one.” — Elara Lin

chapters.title: Love at First Sight Is a Sleep-Deprivation Symptom
chapters.desc: Elara finds her logbook handed to someone else and marches into the chief resident’s office to apologise for being right. He tells her why, and it isn’t a question.
chapters.epigraph: “I can’t take you to dinner and sign your logbook. I picked dinner.” — Wang Xing Yue

chapters.title: Suturing Practice on a Banana
chapters.desc: She beats every student in the skills lab with a needle and a banana. At dinner she talks for three hours, and on the steps outside he stops her in the middle of a story.
chapters.epigraph: “Finish the story later.” — Elara Lin

chapters.title: She Narrates Everything
chapters.desc: A month of noodles at eleven and slow walks to the taxi rank. Then she turns up at his flat with breakfast after his night on call, and doesn’t go home.
chapters.epigraph: “I thought it was sleep deprivation. I gave it fifteen months.” — Wang Xing Yue

chapters.title: The Lins Are Not Told
chapters.desc: For her twenty-third birthday he gives her surgical loupes made for her eyes. She goes to the family dinner without him, and climbs into his car at midnight still in her dress.
chapters.epigraph: “You’re the one part of my life nobody’s ever bled on.” — Elara Lin

chapters.title: Three in the Morning, on Speaker
chapters.desc: Her silent sister rings from a strange phone about a man with an infected knife wound who can’t go to a hospital. For three weeks Elara calls back at three every morning, and Xing Yue writes it all down and never asks who.
chapters.epigraph: “Go back to sleep. I’ve written it down.” — Wang Xing Yue

chapters.title: Zhao Zhendong Is Bleeding Out
chapters.desc: Her sister’s husband crawls home with a bullet in his side, and Elara steals what she needs from the hospital. Xing Yue walks into the supply room and catches her, and she begs him not to ask.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t ask me. If you ask, I’ll tell you.” — Elara Lin

chapters.title: Fifteen Days of Drips
chapters.desc: For two weeks she changes drips and dressings on the hill, and he drives her there in the dark and waits at the bottom of the road. On the last night he asks one question.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not asking who. I only want to know if he’s alive.” — Wang Xing Yue

chapters.title: Every Wrong Answer
chapters.desc: Finals, flashcards in bed and a dare he cheats on. She graduates with her family in the hall, and on the back stairs afterwards he hands her a form already filled in, and she says yes in the middle of a sentence.
chapters.epigraph: “Get it wrong and I’ll kiss you anyway.” — Wang Xing Yue

chapters.title: The Flat on Banyan Terrace
chapters.desc: She starts as an intern across the harbour, living out of a bag, and he hands her the key to a room he’s already finished. She picks the date. On a Friday morning in the old town they marry in secret, with a retired bus driver and a night sister for witnesses.
chapters.epigraph: “Now that’s an answer.” — Mr. Yin

chapters.title: The Cake
chapters.desc: Elara makes four tiers of cake for Elowen’s wedding, and the tall doctor in glasses stands beside it all night while nobody introduces him. At midnight her father asks his name, and he tells him: her husband.
chapters.epigraph: “Sunday. One o’clock. Bring him.” — Lin Jian

chapters.title: Sunday Lunch in the Walled City
chapters.desc: The red door, eleven chairs and a father who has learned to ask things. Raiden asks his intentions, and Xing Yue tells the whole table he’s already married her.
chapters.epigraph: “Does she eat when she’s on nights?” — Lin Jian

chapters.title: An Yu Comes for Tea
chapters.desc: Elara finds out her silent sister got married before she did, and told nobody either. Then his brother flies down for one cup of tea, notices everything, and lets slip how rich the Wangs really are.
chapters.epigraph: “He rang me to ask whether love at first sight was in the literature.” — Wang An Yu

chapters.title: He Is Bad at Holidays
chapters.desc: He works every holiday so other people can go home. On Lunar New Year’s Eve his wife brings dumplings to Ward 9B, and he breaks his own rule.
chapters.epigraph: “I said not in the hospital. I’m allowed to be wrong.” — Wang Xing Yue

chapters.title: Staples on a Kitchen Table
chapters.desc: Her sister shoots a man in a noodle shop, and Elara staples her brother-in-law’s scalp on the kitchen table. She gets home after midnight and shakes on the hall floor, and her husband asks for names.
chapters.epigraph: “Next time ring me first. I’ll drive. I’ll wait in the car.” — Wang Xing Yue

chapters.title: The Vow at Dawn
chapters.desc: On the morning she finishes her intern year he meets her in the old garden at City Hospital and asks his wife to marry him again, in front of everyone this time. She’s talking about fish, and says yes in the middle of a sentence.
chapters.epigraph: “Sorry, what? Say it again. I was talking.” — Elara Lin

chapters.title: The Seventh Guest
chapters.desc: Elara kneels by a river after midnight with her green bag while her husband waits in the car, then runs late up a lane in scrubs to her sister’s garden wedding. That night she says she doesn’t know who her own mother was.
chapters.epigraph: “Ev knows who her mother was now.” — Elara Lin

chapters.title: A Name in a Ledger
chapters.desc: He finds the old matron of the children’s home and the birth name his wife has never heard. He decides to keep it for their garden day, and she catches him hiding something.
chapters.epigraph: “They called her the bell girl. She never stopped.” — Matron Sima

chapters.title: Again?
chapters.desc: At five in the morning her brother and his wife come in from a fire with burned hands. For six weeks she spends her days off fixing switches in the rebuilt shop, humming, and her husband catches her on a ladder.
chapters.epigraph: “You’ve got good hands. Steady. I’d hire you.” — Jinx

chapters.title: The Knife at the Red Door
chapters.desc: After Sunday lunch a man in a seaman’s jacket comes for her father with a knife. Elara gets in the way, and her husband keeps her alive on the stones of the alley, then stands in the corner of theatre with empty hands.
chapters.epigraph: “Stop diagnosing yourself. I know what’s cut.” — Wang Xing Yue

titles.en: The Masterpiece I Could Never Draw

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Raiden Lin plays the cheerful, slightly useless Lin son so well that the Syndicate and the police both ignore him. In fact he draws the family's safe rooms, and knows the weak point of every building in the city. One night he's kneeling in the middle of an illegal race on the old shipyard road, drawing a warehouse, and a motorbike stops two metres from him.

Jinx gets off it to beat some sense into him. He looks up, smiles, and tells her that her intake manifold is beautiful. The next morning he's at her garage near the Docks with three coffees. She drinks all three.

She grew up in a chop shop under the flyover and swore she'd never be owned by anyone again, least of all the Lins. He'd like to marry her. He asks on a napkin, drawn to scale. She says not yet. He keeps asking.

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Raiden is the Lin who talks. In every other book he's in the background, cheerful, drawing something, being an idiot on purpose. I wanted to know what he was like when he stopped pretending, and who would be the first person he did it for. It had to be someone who'd see through him at a hundred and ninety kilometres an hour.

This is the lightest book in the series so far, and the most kissing. They get together in chapter three and never really stop. The trouble isn't whether they'll fall in love. It's her father's shop, his father's name, and two people who were each hidden as children learning to stop hiding each other.

He's rich, and he spoils her: a building, a dyno, a lathe, a hill. She's paying half. She insisted.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a warm, funny romance, but it has some hard moments:

• A man hit by a van, with injuries and a night in hospital (Raiden Gets Hit by a Car)

• A child hidden in a freezer for eleven hours, and a ten-year-old crossing a border alone (Memes at 2 A.M., Ten, Walking Home Alone)

• A threat against a loved one, a knife and an armed crew (Her Father Calls After Five Years, The Men Who Own Her Father, She Builds Her Way Out, Raiden Stops Playing Dumb)

• A remembered attempted assault on a teenage girl, which she fought off; not shown on the page (Her Father Says Sorry, She Lets Him In)

• A friend coming back injured, and grief and fear (The Masterpiece He Could Never Draw)

• A workshop fire and smoke inhalation (The Fire at the Shop)

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
The black door — Jinx's first garage, near the Iron Docks, under an old sign that says TAI HING ROPE & CANVAS.
The shipyard road — Two kilometres of cracked concrete between the dead shipyard and the cranes. Illegal races at one in the morning.
Mrs. Tong's — The noodle place on the corner that only serves men off the container ships. The table by the fridge, back to the wall.
The Meridian — Raiden's glass tower in the Symmetrical Ward. Thirty-one floors. The desk man calls the pale green bike “the tram”.
The pale green bike — The one Jinx built him. Twenty kilometres an hour, lights like a train, a drawing board on the tank, a bell.
The steel room — Behind her tool wall. A light that comes on by itself, air, a line out, a warm lamp she added, and a tin of peaches.
The napkins — Thirty-one proposals, each drawn to scale, kept in his wallet where other people keep photographs.
Under the flyover — The Slums of the Industry, where the sun never gets in. Her father's shop, CAO MOTOR REPAIR.
The gap — Behind the scrap heap, between the wall and the pillar. On the archive drawings from 1974.
The triple — A 1973 two-stroke, three cylinders, a widowmaker. Seized for seven years. Ran at 5:40 a.m.
Oh-three-one-one — The day she left. The code to everything she owns.
JINX — The shop in the old chandler's warehouse three doors down, with a long low window anyone can see into. The sign she cut herself.
The stair — Behind the third shelf on the mezzanine. Two hours of fire board. Used once.
The driveway — One point two kilometres on the hill above the reservoir road. It is a racetrack.
The monkey — The passenger in a racing sidecar, who hangs off the side. Raiden says navigator.
Dyno — A rolling road that measures a bike's power at the back wheel.
Intake manifold — The pipes that carry air and fuel into the engine. Hers are all the same length, by hand.

chapters.title: Sketching in the Middle of a Race Track
chapters.desc: May 2021. Jinx is testing a new intake on the old shipyard road when a man kneels down in front of her to draw a warehouse. She stops in time. Then she nearly kills him anyway.
chapters.epigraph: “I didn’t hit him. Write that down. I want it on record that I didn’t hit him.” — Jinx

chapters.title: “Nice Intake Manifold” Is Not a Pick-Up Line
chapters.desc: The man from the road turns up at her garage the next morning with a drawing and three coffees. She drinks all three, tells him no all day, and somehow ends up saying Thursday.
chapters.epigraph: “I brought three because I didn’t know how you took it. Now I know. You take all three.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: The Socialite Everyone Ignores
chapters.desc: Their first date is a gallery opening forty-one floors up, where he plays the fool so well the whole room believes him. On the back stairs he tells her his surname, and she goes home to choose a spanner.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody shoots the boy who can’t find his own coat.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: The First Kiss Smells Like Oil
chapters.desc: She throws the spanner and misses on purpose. Under her bike, on two creepers, he makes a rule about her real name and begs his way right up to the edge of it.
chapters.epigraph: “I said I’d go if you threw a spanner. I didn’t say what happens if you miss.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Raiden Gets Hit by a Car
chapters.desc: June 2021. She’s forty minutes late to pick him up, and a van finds him first. She sits up all night at City Hospital, and at dawn he begs her to leave by the back before his family arrives. She goes.
chapters.epigraph: “I was on the pavement. I promise. I was on the pavement.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: A Bike That Goes Twenty Kilometres an Hour
chapters.desc: She ignores him for three weeks, and Zhao Zhendong turns up at her door with her jacket. Then she builds a pale green bike that can’t go faster than twenty, rides it into his tower, and finds out what he was really afraid of.
chapters.epigraph: “If you’re going to draw in roads, you do it on this.” — Jinx

chapters.title: Her Father’s Chop Shop
chapters.desc: August 2021. She takes him to a roof across the lane from her father’s chop shop under the flyover and tells him some of it. She won’t go down. He goes home and maps every way out.
chapters.epigraph: “First word I ever read was torque.” — Jinx

chapters.title: He Asks Her to Marry Him on a Napkin Drawing
chapters.desc: September 2021. At Mrs. Tong’s he slides a napkin across the table with their whole life drawn on it to scale. She says yes, on conditions, and they sign the terms in chilli oil. Then she has thirteen days to break every rule he makes.
chapters.epigraph: “Yes. A registry. Not your father’s house.” — Jinx

chapters.title: The Trophy Husband Has Dinner Ready
chapters.desc: They marry at the old-town registry with two washers for rings and Mrs. Tong crying louder than anyone. Then her husband moves into her two rooms with a wok, saves her in his phone as Tyres, and loses an argument about dumplings.
chapters.epigraph: “Somebody has to cook. You’d put soup in a gearbox if I let you.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: The Roof That Will Never Fall
chapters.desc: Winter 2021 to spring 2022. A letter says her building has been sold, and it has, to her. Her husband spends New Year at his father’s table with his ring on a string, then spends three months building the napkin, with steel in every wall.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s in your name. Only yours. I’m sorry. I know I promised I’d only use it when it was important.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: The Meanest Engineer in the City
chapters.desc: April 2022. At a charity gala full of people who know his father, a racing driver with kitchen-scissor hair catches him looking at a crack. By the end of the night she knows he’s married, and Jinx has a new client who pays in gearboxes.
chapters.epigraph: “She could build a bike faster than you could crash it. I’d bet money. I’d bet your money.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Raiden Is Proud of Her for an Entire Week
chapters.desc: October 2022. Her black bike wins Best in Show up north, and her husband tells a petrol station, a toll booth and an entire bus. He tells everyone except his own family. Then he tells Zhao, and Zhao already knows.
chapters.epigraph: “I’d like everyone to know. I’d like a plane to write it in the sky. I’ve looked into it. It’s very expensive and the wind spoils the letters.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Memes at 2 A.M.
chapters.desc: December 2022. Her husband can’t sleep, so he sends her memes from the next pillow. She works out why before he does. A farm in the borderland, a freezer, eleven hours, and a light she puts in for him.
chapters.epigraph: “You built me a freezer with the light on.” — Jinx

chapters.title: Ten, Walking Home Alone
chapters.desc: January 2023. How a boy of ten copied a road map onto his arm, crossed a border under the ice in a fish truck, and knocked on his father’s door six days later. Then, at two in the morning, she rides to the Walled City for the first time to see that door.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody was coming. So I went to them.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: A Commission From the Syndicate
chapters.desc: June 2023. She finds drawings on his table for a house on the Peak, with a steel room inside it, and the client’s initials in the corner. They have their first real fight as husband and wife, and they don’t finish it. Then he asks her to a wedding.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody looks at me. That’s the whole point.” “I looked.” — Raiden Lin and Jinx

chapters.title: Jinx Meets the Lin Family Properly
chapters.desc: September 2023. Elowen’s wedding in the flower shop: thirty people standing, a father in his funeral suit, four sisters. “Jinx, my wife, she built Xiao Pan’s bike, don’t touch her tools.” Two years of secret marriage, out in one sentence, and one silent sister who nods.
chapters.epigraph: “You were the little girl under the bench. With the carburettor. I’ve always wondered what happened to you.” — Lin Jian

chapters.title: Her Father Calls After Five Years
chapters.desc: Autumn 2023. A secret car built at night for a friend, and a husband who comes down at two in the morning with soup and asks nothing. Then, in November, a phone call from under the flyover, a photograph of an old camp bed, and a note on the bench.
chapters.epigraph: “Gone to see my father. Don’t come. Back tomorrow.” — a note on the bench, in biro, on the back of an invoice

chapters.title: The Men Who Own Her Father
chapters.desc: Under the flyover: a polite man in reading glasses, a debt to be paid in stolen bikes, and a dead brother’s motorbike that hasn’t run in nine years. Then her useless husband wanders in through the scrap heap with a bag of dumplings and a floor plan in his jacket.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m terribly sorry. I think I’m lost. Is this the right flyover?” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: She Builds Her Way Out
chapters.desc: One night, one engine, three cylinders that haven’t moved in years. Her husband holds the torch, her father comes out of the office to point at the wrong jet, and just before six the widowmaker coughs.
chapters.epigraph: “Lie to it. Just this once. We’ll fix it properly after.” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Raiden Stops Playing Dumb
chapters.desc: Just before six in the morning under the flyover, the deal is broken and a knife comes out. Her useless husband steps in front of her and stops pretending. Then a black car at the end of the lane, and a brother-in-law who owes him one.
chapters.epigraph: “I know every building in this district. I know yours. You added two floors in 2019 on a frame drawn for four. Shall I tell you which beam?” — Raiden Lin

chapters.title: Her Father Says Sorry
chapters.desc: Winter 2023 into 2024. Her father sits on the black step and says sorry, badly. Then the red door opens for her at last, she refuses Lin Jian a favour in his own kitchen, and at New Year she kisses her husband on his father’s roof in front of everyone.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody has said no to me in my own kitchen since 1987. Sit down. Eat. You’re my daughter-in-law.” — Lin Jian

chapters.title: She Lets Him In
chapters.desc: March 2024. The thing that happened when she was seventeen, a steel cabinet she’s had since she left, and its code. Then the thirty-first napkin, two creepers under a bike, to scale, and a yes. Then a wedding at Mrs. Tong’s on a Thursday, the one his family can come to, and a bike show up north in their good clothes.
chapters.epigraph: “Oh-three-one-one. The day I left. It’s the code to everything I own that’s mine.” — Jinx

descs.en: He blew open a shipping container expecting guns and found a princess. She won’t go home. She keeps coming back.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Lee Jun Hyuk goes to West Basin at two in the morning to kill the man who signs the papers. He blows the lock on the wrong container, expecting guns, and finds five women who have been in the dark for two days. One of them is standing in the middle of the box, between the door and the others, with her hands open.

He gets them out, leaves them at a hospital, and won't give his name. Evangeline Lin finds him anyway: a noodle menu on a dashboard, three days at a corner table, two bowls ordered every time. She is the Lin family's quiet daughter, the paper twin, and she has been somebody's secret since she was three days old. He is a big, kind, talkative man who hunts the people who move people, and he has a rule about everything.

She follows all of his rules except one. She keeps coming back.

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Evangeline says almost nothing in Every Flower in the Shop. I always wanted to know what she'd say if somebody waited long enough, and the answer turned out to be: not much, and every word of it on purpose. So I gave her the man who talks more than anyone in the series. He talks to frightened people so they'll follow his voice. She's the first person who ever listened to all of it.

It's a dark book in places. He's done terrible things for what he thinks are good reasons, and the book doesn't pretend otherwise. But it's mostly about small things done in dangerous rooms: towels folded in thirds, a lamp left on, a window box behind bulletproof glass, a man practising a woman's name in the shower. And about what happens when the one person who never asks for anything finally asks.

He's rich, by the way. Very. He just never had anyone to spend it on. That changes in chapter fourteen, and then it really changes.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a dark romance with a lot of tenderness in it, but it has hard moments:

• Human trafficking: women held in a shipping container, and a lorry where eleven women died (The Container Had a Princess in It, Don't Stop Moving, She Asks Nothing, Someone Else Finishes It)

• Killings by the hero, mostly off the page (Don't Stop Moving, He Goes Hunting)

• An infected knife wound and a high fever, treated at home (The Night He Had a Fever)

• A dying man and morphine (The Target Is a Judge)

• A photograph of a captive sold online (The Traffickers Remember Her)

• A knife held to a father's throat, with no harm done (Jun Hyuk Meets His Father-in-Law (Badly))

• An abduction attempt, a head injury and a shooting (The Abduction Attempt, She Shoots First, After)

• A man found in a refrigerated container (Jun Hyuk Takes a Job He Hates)

• A sniper's choice on a riverbank (He Goes Anyway — Then Turns Back)

• A mother's death in an aid station, remembered by a child (The Borderland Boy)

• Grief for a parent the heroine never knew (A Letter From a Palace, The Throne Lets Her Go)

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
West Basin — The container terminal where it starts. Row K, the old control tower.
Nam's Noodles — Eleven tables on River Bridge Road in the border town. Phones go in a jar between the chilli oil and the soy sauce.
The karaoke flat — Two rooms over a karaoke bar that closed in 2019. Painted windows, three locks, a camp bed.
The menu — Nam's takeaway menu, taped inside the door, with his rules on the back (and two of hers).
The textile building — Eight storeys by the harbour. He owns it. Sixth floor: five windows of glass you can shoot at all day.
The window box — A steel greenhouse bolted to a twenty-centimetre ledge, behind a hatch cut into bulletproof glass.
The rabbit book — His school exercise book of names, boats and payments. There are ten in the end.
The Grey Lanterns — The border unit that took him in at eight. Old Ko's unit.
The court language — The language of the country she was born in, which is never named. She taught herself.
The heron — The gold crest on her baby blanket: a heron over three peaks.
No. 9 Fig Tree Lane — The house with a real address. Thirty-one windows, and every one of them opens.
The Open Door — The foundation she starts for people who come out of boxes.
Rule seven — Don't come back.

chapters.title: The Container Had a Princess in It
chapters.desc: He went to West Basin to kill the man who signs the papers. On the way, he opens the wrong box.
chapters.epigraph: “If you want to live, stay behind me.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, row K, West Basin container terminal

chapters.title: Don’t Stop Moving
chapters.desc: She runs through the stacks holding a stranger’s hand while he talks the whole way. He goes up a tower for four minutes, and she counts every second of them.
chapters.epigraph: “If I’m not back in four minutes, you’re in charge. You look like you’re already in charge.”

chapters.title: He Leaves Her at a Hospital
chapters.desc: Harbourside General, three in the morning. He won’t give her his name, and he doesn’t look back. She keeps his jacket anyway.
chapters.epigraph: “Name.” “No.” — the emergency entrance, Harbourside General

chapters.title: Evangeline Does Not Go Home
chapters.desc: Her father sends a car to the hospital, and for the first time in her life she sends it back. Then, before dawn, she asks Zhao Zhendong one question.
chapters.epigraph: “No.” — Evangeline Lin, to her father, for the first time in twenty-four years

chapters.title: The Woman Who Kept Showing Up
chapters.desc: Three days at a corner table in a noodle shop by the river bridge, two bowls every time. On the fourth day he comes in out of the rain and sits down at the cold one.
chapters.epigraph: “She orders two bowls. Every time. One for her and one that goes cold. I’ve stopped charging her for the cold one.” — Old Nam, River Bridge Road

chapters.title: Lee Jun Hyuk Does Not Own Towels
chapters.desc: He dries himself with yesterday’s T-shirt, so she brings him three white towels. On a Sunday she catches him folding them wrong, and he asks if he can kiss her.
chapters.epigraph: “You own something, you have to go back for it. Old Ko said that. Old Ko owned one spoon.”

chapters.title: Rules of a Safe House
chapters.desc: He comes home in the middle of the night with another man’s blood on his sleeve and finds the lamp still on. So he writes her seven rules on the back of a noodle menu. She keeps six.
chapters.epigraph: “7. Don’t come back.” — the back of a menu from Nam’s Noodles, taped to the inside of a door

chapters.title: She Watches the Exits
chapters.desc: Feet on the stairs, the lamp already off, and a back window he thought nobody knew about. She got there first. Then, in Nam’s back room, she tells him what she was raised to be.
chapters.epigraph: “Every house has a place where the sound carries. I’d found them all by the time I was seven.”

chapters.title: The Night He Had a Fever
chapters.desc: A knife wound he stitched himself, a week of lying about it, and a fever of forty degrees. For once he can’t talk, so she does, all night.
chapters.epigraph: “When people are scared, you keep talking, so they hear a voice that isn’t scared, and they follow the voice.” — Sergeant Ko Baek-san, who never met her

chapters.title: Four Syllables
chapters.desc: Three weeks of healing, a spoon for a birthday that isn’t one, and a man who has gone quiet for the first time in his life. He practises four syllables in the shower. She decides the rest.
chapters.epigraph: “That’s not a name. That’s a sentence.” — Lee Jun Hyuk, October, before he learned it

chapters.title: A Silver Ring With Coordinates Inside
chapters.desc: Nam has bought a hat and he still hasn’t asked. On Friday night he puts a ring beside her teacup, on Saturday a clerk by the bridge stamps the form, and that night she finds out why he was in such a hurry.
chapters.epigraph: “If I don’t come back, this ring has the coordinates to a life where no one can find you. If I do come back, you’re mine.”

chapters.title: The Target Is a Judge
chapters.desc: He comes home from across the river with honey and no Ferryman. In June he climbs the stairs to the flat of the judge who let the Ferryman go, and finds an old man who has been waiting for him since March.
chapters.epigraph: “I wondered when you’d come. I’ve been leaving the door unlocked since March.” — Judge Lo Wing-hang

chapters.title: She Asks Nothing
chapters.desc: In the dark, with her hand on his chest, her husband tells her about a truck on the river road in 2015 and waits for her to leave. Two nights later the typhoon takes the power, and she lights the three candles from the drawer.
chapters.epigraph: “You opened mine.” — Evangeline, in the dark, on the twenty-second of June

chapters.title: Elowen Visits, Carrying Groceries
chapters.desc: Elowen comes up the border road with four bags of shopping and a dozen lemons from their mother’s tree, and finally asks about the ring. Down on the bridge, her husband waits in a car, and Jun Hyuk goes to say hello.
chapters.epigraph: “I married a man who says one word. You found one who says all of them.” — Elowen Zhao

chapters.title: Evangeline Wants a Window Box
chapters.desc: People are asking about him at the border, so in August her husband moves them to a sixth-floor flat in the city with a real stove and windows nobody can shoot through. They don’t open. She mentions basil once.
chapters.epigraph: “Basil would grow there.” — Evangeline, not asking for anything

chapters.title: He Builds One Anyway
chapters.desc: A steel box bolted to a ledge six floors up, a hatch cut into bulletproof glass, and nine pots of herbs. Then a pair of earrings from Harbour Road and Elowen’s flower-shop wedding, where Evangeline stands at the back and her husband watches from a roof across the street.
chapters.epigraph: “Good mend.” — Evangeline Lin, at a wedding, to Aurelia Chen

chapters.title: The Traffickers Remember Her
chapters.desc: October is basil and a ridiculous blue coat. Then Eliana finds the only photograph of Evangeline in the world, taken with a flash inside a container, for sale.
chapters.epigraph: “Price on request. Serious buyers only. Palace interest welcome.” — a listing, deleted at 4:00 a.m.

chapters.title: He Goes Hunting
chapters.desc: A mahjong club above a car wash on Kiln Street, a man called Hwang, and four days. She follows every rule her husband ever wrote. She doesn’t sleep.
chapters.epigraph: “If I’m not back by Sunday, go to your sister. Don’t wait up.” “I won’t.” — the sixth floor, Thursday night

chapters.title: She Washes His Hands
chapters.desc: Warm water, a nail brush and ten fingers, one at a time. She doesn’t ask whose it is. When he finally wakes, he tells her the only part she needs: who answered the advertisement.
chapters.epigraph: “Why don’t you ask?” “Because you’d tell me.”

descs.en: She saw through the guard nobody else noticed. He has spent ten years making people disappear, and now he wants to disappear with her.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
At a government reception on Battery Hill, sixty guards stand at the doors and look at the guests. One of them doesn’t. He watches a single man for forty-one minutes, and the only person in the building who notices is Serafina Song, there on a staff pass to inspect a red Lancia, in her sister’s dress and her own boots.

She walks across the ballroom and tells him he isn’t a guard. She’s right. Qin Haozhen has spent ten years making people disappear for a state that doesn’t put its name on doors, and nobody has ever looked at him before.

She finds his name with one bribed caterer. She asks him for a race, not a date. And a man who sleeps four hours a night in any bed in any country falls asleep in the passenger seat of her thirty-year-old car at three in the morning, and keeps coming back.

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Serafina walked out of her engagement dinner between the soup and the fish in The Woman Who Sets the Price, and then turned up at her sister’s wedding in Milan with oil on her boots. I always wanted to know who could keep up with her.

The answer turned out to be the most forgettable man in the room. Haozhen is not a good man at the start of this book, and it doesn’t pretend he is. It’s about a man finding out he’s allowed to want something, starting with an egg sandwich, and a woman who decides every single morning whether she can live with the truth about him, and keeps deciding yes.

The racing is as real as I could make it: braking markers, tyre temperatures, driver changes, telemetry in four coloured lines. The spy work stays at the level of a story. And yes, the car really can do two hundred miles an hour. He did the brakes.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a fast, funny book, but it has some hard moments:

• A state operative’s work, including abductions and killings, mostly off the page and remembered (What He Does for Work, The Target Has a Family, Chen Si Brokers a Truce)

• A man taken from his family in front of his young son (The Target Has a Family)

• Trauma, depression and silence after a mission (He Comes Home Wrong)

• A cruel parent and a family’s financial collapse (The Song Family Opposes the Match)

• Threats against family members and surveillance (A File on the Workbench)

• A car chase, gunfire, a gunshot wound and a burning car (Shoot the Tyres), and a fever (The Safe House in the Mountains)

• Wound stitching without a doctor (The First Time He Bleeds in Her Garage)

• A serious racing crash, intensive care and a long recovery from concussion (The Needle, Hospital, Night Two, She Drives Again)

• Illegal street racing throughout Volume One

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
Nonna — Serafina’s red 1992 Lancia Delta HF Integrale, named after their grandmother.
Gilded — Team AURELIA’s matte black race car, number 7, with AURELIA in gold on the bonnet.
Nobody — The getaway car: a grey 2006 Toyota Crown estate with wooden-bead seat covers and an engine it should never have had.
Two Hundred — A burnt-out 1991 endurance prototype, bought for scrap.
The garage — Under the railway bridge in the industrial district. Trains every eleven minutes.
Granny Shum’s — The Saturday street races by the paint works: the long straight, the S-bends, the lamp posts round the gas works.
The Needle — The hairpin at the end of the back straight at the circuit in the north.
The Eleventh — The Bureau Haozhen worked for, in a building with no name on it.
Brake on the marker — Braking exactly at the board, to the metre.
Telemetry — The car’s data: speed, throttle, brake and steering, a thousand times a second.

chapters.title: The Guard Nobody Else Noticed
chapters.desc: Serafina is on Battery Hill to check a car for a forged plate, and she spots a guard who isn’t guarding anyone. So she walks over and tells him.
chapters.epigraph: “Everyone in that room was looking at somebody. He was the only one looking at the right person.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: Serafina Finds Out His Name
chapters.desc: Three weeks, one bribed caterer and a note about his terrible brakes. Then the guard turns up in her garage in the middle of the night to ask her to stop.
chapters.epigraph: “A car tells you everything about the man who drives it. His just told me to mind my own business.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: A Race, Not a Date
chapters.desc: She makes him race her at Granny Shum’s, his grey taxi of a car against her Lancia. He loses on purpose, and she’s furious about it.
chapters.epigraph: “A circuit is a circuit and a road is a road, and I’m not giving up the road for anybody.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: Rematch
chapters.desc: A track day in the north, one car, two drivers and Mouse on the stopwatch. This time he drives like himself, and she kisses him in the empty paddock.
chapters.epigraph: “Five laps each, same car, Mouse on the clock. Then we both know.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: 3 A.M., Passenger Seat
chapters.desc: He hasn’t slept properly in ten years. Then he falls asleep in her passenger seat, and she drives round the harbour till dawn so he won’t wake up.
chapters.epigraph: “In ten years I’ve never sat in a car I wasn’t driving or guarding.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: What He Does for Work
chapters.desc: Mouse finds the missing Belgian in a newspaper. Serafina lays out everything she knows on the workbench, and he doesn’t tell her she’s wrong.
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t lie to you. I’ve never lied to you. I just haven’t told you most of it.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: She Should Run
chapters.desc: She knows exactly how to run. Instead she turns up outside his flat at six in the morning with two egg sandwiches and four rules.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not going to run. I’m the one people run with.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: The First Time He Bleeds in Her Garage
chapters.desc: He’s late for Valentine’s dinner because of a knife in a stairwell. She stitches his arm with fishing line and swears the whole way through.
chapters.epigraph: “Rule two doesn’t cover blood. Sit down before you fall on my car.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: Twelve Days and a Postcard
chapters.desc: He’s gone for twelve days with no phone. She nearly puts Gilded into the tyre wall, Aurelia notices, and then a postcard comes with nothing written on it.
chapters.epigraph: “When you can tell me, tell me. That’s how it works in my house.” — Aurelia Chen

chapters.title: The Ring Was in the Glovebox
chapters.desc: She goes into his glovebox for the tyre gauge and finds a ring. He had a speech in four parts, and she says yes before he gets to part two.
chapters.epigraph: “I had a plan. It had four parts. You were supposed to let me finish.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: Qin Haozhen Has Never Planned a Party
chapters.desc: He has stood at the door of eleven weddings and never been inside one, so he makes a list. Then he puts the engagement on a Bureau form, forgets his own toast, and she buys a burnt-out race car for scrap.
chapters.epigraph: “Depends how many people love you. Start counting.” — Mr. Kwok

chapters.title: Aurelia Finds Out Who Pays for the Racing Team
chapters.desc: Aurelia does the team’s books and finds sixty thousand she didn’t pay. At Da Gianni the whole restaurant hears whose salary bought Sera’s gearbox.
chapters.epigraph: “He overpaid by a third. I like him.” — Aurelia Chen

chapters.title: Two Professionals at One Table
chapters.desc: Dinner on the forty-fourth floor. Two men go for the same chair, the ruby moves to the right finger, and Chen Si takes Haozhen out on the balcony.
chapters.epigraph: “Mr. Qin. Welcome. You don’t exist.” — Qian

chapters.title: Director Duan Sends Congratulations
chapters.desc: His director has read the form. She brings congratulations, a silver pen with a 7 on it, and a folder for Lisbon. Serafina uses the pen to enter a hill climb.
chapters.epigraph: “We look after our families. It’s in the training.” — Director Duan Qiuyan

chapters.title: Five A.M., Departures
chapters.desc: The last night before Lisbon, then the airport at five in the morning. She gives him her grandmother’s tyre gauge, and he says it through the car window.
chapters.epigraph: “You have to bring it back. It’s the only one that reads true. I’ll need it for the hill climb.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: Baizhang Pass
chapters.desc: She races up a mountain without her gauge. On the other side of the world, a man and a night porter watch the stream at four in the morning.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s a waste of good tyres. His tyres.” — Big Wu

chapters.title: The Target Has a Family
chapters.desc: Lisbon. Twenty-three days in a chair by a door, counting a boy’s keepy-ups. Then the job.
chapters.epigraph: “Not in front of the house. Please. That’s my son’s window.” — Gong Ruiming

chapters.title: He Comes Home Wrong
chapters.desc: He comes home, sits in her passenger seat and says nothing for two days. Her father’s company is falling apart, and in the end he tells her about the boy.
chapters.epigraph: “I’m not going to ask. I’m going to sit here. You talk when there’s something you can say.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: The Song Family Opposes the Match
chapters.desc: Her mother writes for the first time in seven years: bring him. The house on the Peak has lot numbers on everything, and her mother asks him nine questions.
chapters.epigraph: “Nobody keeps her, madam. I’d like to be wherever she is. That’s all I’m asking for.” — Qin Haozhen

chapters.title: Jinx Builds the Getaway Car
chapters.desc: Rule four, at the kettle: he wants out. That means a car nobody knows, so they go to Jinx.
chapters.epigraph: “One order. No questions. And you never bring it back here with a hole in it.” — Jinx

chapters.title: The Mission He Didn’t Take
chapters.desc: A grey building in the capital that isn’t on any map. A seventh-floor office with a radiator that knocks. A thin folder about a journalist in Singapore. For the first time in eleven years, he says one word to the state, and it’s the wrong one.
chapters.epigraph: “Do you know what happens to people who say no, Haozhen?” “Yes, Director. I’ve driven them.”

descs.en: She proposed with eleven pages of terms. Clause nine is about the bedroom. Clause ten is a single word.

titles.en: The Woman Who Sets the Price

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
On the night of her father’s birthday, in front of two hundred guests, Aurelia Song’s mother raises a glass and announces that her daughter’s jewellery boutique is losing four million a year and will close in January. Aurelia walks out onto the balcony in gold silk, shaking, doing sums in her head. A stranger at the far end gives her his coat.

Six weeks later, the stranger walks into her boutique and asks to rent it. His name is Chen Si. He runs the Syndicate. He wants her shop for his business. She sets a price instead: a seat at his table.

Then she proposes. Eleven pages, in red ink, with terms. Clause nine is about the bedroom. Clause ten is a single word.

Between them stand a mother who loves only winners, a vice-minister who framed his father, a poisoned glass of wine on New Year’s Eve, a traitor at the table, and a woman who has never once in her life been loved without having to win.

The Woman Who Sets the Price is a sharp, glamorous, power-couple romance about a queen who refuses to be a title, and a man who never once asks her to win.

The main story is told across four volumes and is complete. Side stories at the end can be read any time. Aurelia and Chen Si first appear in Every Flower in the Shop and Proof by Induction, but this book stands on its own.

21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This book has some dark moments:

• A parent who humiliates her daughter in public, and emotional coercion within a family

• Organised crime, with threats and violence mostly off the page, and a car attack (A Snake in the Syndicate)

• A poisoning, intensive care and a long recovery (Volume Three)

• A panic attack and its aftermath, and therapy (The Word Is Milan)

• Memories of a parent’s wrongful arrest and death in custody, and of a riot and a stabbing in a juvenile detention centre (The Sewer, Nineteen Years Ago)

• Consensual power-play love scenes between a married couple, with a contract, orders, blindfolds, silk ties and a safe word. They are sensual but not explicit

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Aurelia Song was the rival in Every Flower in the Shop: gold, sunglasses, a slap in the rain, a running score. I wanted to know who she was at two in the morning, when nobody was watching her walk. This is her book.

The crime is kept at the level of a story; nothing here is a how-to. The jewellery is as real as I could make it: piercing saws, gravers, box links soldered one at a time, rouge on the wheel for the last pass.

Thank you for reading. Second is just the first of the ones who kept going.

glossary.title: Names & Terms
glossary.content:
AURELIA — Aurelia’s jewellery boutique on Harbour Road.
The Syndicate — The organisation Chen Si runs. Thirty years old, and older than him.
The terms — Aurelia’s price for laundering money through her shop: a share, real pieces, the books, no lies, a seat at the table.
The marriage agreement — Eleven clauses, renewable after ten years, when the Wife may rewrite every one. At the renewal, he adds a twelfth and a thirteenth.
Clause twelve — The Wife is not the Husband’s queen.
The word — The safe word written into the agreement. It is “Milan.”
Numero Uno — The necklace she named at two in the morning, after a phone call with her mother.
The Jade Hall — A restaurant on Temple Street with a round table for twelve. It has belonged to the Syndicate for thirty years.
The house on the Peak — Her parents’ house, where the party for her father’s fifty-seventh birthday was held.
The Song Group — Her father’s company.
The Pearl — The restaurant booked for New Year’s Eve, same as always.
Tesoro — Her father’s name for her, from before Vienna.

chapters.title: The Balcony Where He Lent Her His Coat
chapters.desc: Her mother closes her shop in the middle of a birthday toast. Out on the balcony, a stranger lends her his coat and doesn’t try to make it better.
chapters.epigraph: “The world is obsessed with your shine. I’m more interested in what you do in the dark.”

chapters.title: The Man Who Wanted to Rent Her Shop
chapters.desc: He comes to her shop offering to wash his money through it. She hands him back his own letter, covered in red ink.
chapters.epigraph: “You want my shop. I want a seat at your table. Those are the terms.”

chapters.title: Aurelia Negotiates a Don Into a Corner
chapters.desc: She takes him to a basement with no menu and finds a thief in his books before the fish goes cold. Under a streetlamp, he stops waiting.
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t drink things people give me. I drink things I take.”

chapters.title: Aurelia Song Does Not Do Second Place
chapters.desc: The men who run his routes take away her chairs, so she sits in his. Then she kisses him in it and wins every hand of mahjong in the building.
chapters.epigraph: “Rule one of a room full of men who want you gone: sit down first.”

chapters.title: The First Ledger She Ever Read
chapters.desc: Her first crate gets through customs at dawn, and she loves every minute. That night at her counter he looks at her mouth, and leaves.
chapters.epigraph: “It isn’t that I like breaking rules. I like knowing exactly which ones I’m breaking, and what they cost.”

chapters.title: He Never Asks Her to Win
chapters.desc: She loses a game of chess on purpose to see what he’ll do. He lays down his own king.
chapters.epigraph: “I don’t care if you win, Aurelia. I don’t care if you lose. You could lose every game you ever play me and I’d just want another one.”

chapters.title: Dinner on the Forty-Fourth Floor
chapters.desc: He cooks her dinner and tells her how his parents died. Then she tells him to kneel, and he does.
chapters.epigraph: “Take off your watch. I don’t want you counting.”

chapters.title: A Proposal With Terms and Conditions
chapters.desc: She proposes with eleven pages of red ink. He signs every one, and writes something in the margin she can’t argue with.
chapters.epigraph: “Clause 9. In private, the Wife sets the terms, unless and until she says otherwise. Clause 10. The word is ‘Milan’.”

chapters.title: The Song Parents Are Not Told
chapters.desc: She marries him in Milan with eleven guests and the sister she hasn’t spoken to in two years, and lets her mother find out from Vogue.
chapters.epigraph: “Shouldn’t we tell your parents?” “We will. They read Italian Vogue.”

chapters.title: Blood Brothers at the Reception
chapters.desc: Zhao makes a nine-word speech and Serafina offers her a getaway car. On the wedding night, the bride blindfolds her husband with her veil.
chapters.epigraph: “He is my brother. You’re his. So you’re mine.” — the complete best man’s speech of Zhao Zhendong

chapters.title: A Necklace on the Hit List
chapters.desc: She finishes the best necklace she’s ever made and drapes it over her husband’s shoulders while he stares at his list. He makes her count the stones out loud.
chapters.epigraph: “My King. You’ve been staring at that list for an hour. Everyone on it, put together, is worth less than this necklace.”

chapters.title: Chen Si Lost an Argument (Once)
chapters.desc: A grey car follows her, and he wants two men behind her everywhere. She wins the argument with a cancelled shipment, three days at Zhao’s range and a page of red ink.
chapters.epigraph: “He lost. Good.” — Zhao Zhendong

chapters.title: The Song Family Is Coming to Dinner
chapters.desc: Her mother writes to invite herself to dinner. Chen Si cooks the fish, Aurelia leaves the dishwasher whining on purpose, and at the door her mother names the one man he can’t stand.
chapters.epigraph: “Your father and I would like to come to dinner. We would like to be proud of you.” — Vittoria Song, letter, 2 October

chapters.title: What Her Father Wants
chapters.desc: Over risotto at Da Gianni, her father asks Chen Si to write to Fu Jianguo. Then he admits he’s already told Fu no.
chapters.epigraph: “It’s only a letter. A few lines. Your name at the bottom. It would mean so much.” — Song Weiren

chapters.title: Aurelia Says No to Her Mother
chapters.desc: She tells her mother no in front of the maids. Then she and Mr. Lu work out how to get at Fu through his son.
chapters.epigraph: “No, Mamma. Not for the bridge. Not for you. Not ever.” — in Italian, so the maids understood too

chapters.title: Her Mother’s Last Card
chapters.desc: Her mother sends a photograph of Serafina at a street race and names her price. Aurelia keeps it from Chen Si for one night and goes to the garage under the railway bridge.
chapters.epigraph: “You have something I want, tesoro. And I have your sister.”

chapters.title: The Racing Team She Pretends Not to Fund
chapters.desc: Aurelia sells Fu Kang a watch from Geneva and follows his money all the way to his father’s name. She also learns to change a wheel and rebuilds her sister’s sponsorship deck in one night.
chapters.epigraph: “You don’t pretend to fund it any more.” “No. Now I pretend I’m not terrified.”

chapters.title: Sisters at a Racetrack
chapters.desc: Serafina wins the last race of the season with AURELIA on her bonnet. Chen Si goes up to the VIP lounge to have a word with her mother.
chapters.epigraph: “Don’t watch the car. Watch the gap. The car goes where the gap is.” — Serafina Song

chapters.title: My Queen Is Not a Title
chapters.desc: Aurelia wears a dress of gold to her mother’s Christmas party, and Chen Si calls her his queen in front of Fu Jianguo. Upstairs, in her old room, he makes her watch herself in the mirror.
chapters.epigraph: “She doesn’t need my name. She has her own.” — Chen Si

chapters.title: A Snake in the Syndicate
chapters.desc: Someone parks a lorry across the coast road in front of Zhao’s car. Chen Si comes home with shaking hands, knowing Sun Wei sold his diary, and decides to go to Sun Wei’s New Year’s Eve dinner anyway.
chapters.epigraph: “Zhendong doesn’t brake.” — Chen Si

descs.en: He made a rule: the two of them stay flat, like a line on a graph. She has a calendar with 266 squares, and she has no intention of waiting for the last one.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Dr. Miles Wei, 31, lecturer in physics, holds office hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Shen Yu Jie, final-year student and the best mind in the department, comes on Wednesdays. Every Wednesday. With problems she has already solved.

He has one rule: nothing happens while she is a student in his department. He draws it on his chalkboard as a flat line. She adds an end date. 20 June, 16:00. Then she makes a calendar, two hundred and sixty-six squares long, and draws a physically inaccurate atom in every one.

Between them stand sticky-note physics jokes, a department that has started a betting pool, a supervisor who smokes on a balcony she isn’t allowed on, a mother who calls her daughter the Perfect Jewel in front of guests, a diplomat with a secret, and a grant nobody applied for.

Proof by Induction is a bright, slow-burn campus romance about waiting, about being taken seriously, and about a man who stopped laughing at seventeen and a woman who makes him start again.

The main story is told across four volumes and is complete. Side stories at the end can be read any time. Miles first appears as a side character in Every Flower in the Shop, but this book stands on its own.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
21+ · For adult readers. Mature themes and heated love scenes.

This is a gentle book, but it has some hard moments:

• Emotional control and coercion by a parent, including being cut off financially and made to leave home (Volume Two and Volume Three)

• Online gossip and sexist rumours about a student (Rumours in the Department Kitchen)

• A character coming out to his family at a dinner table, and a parent walking out (The Perfect Jewel Says No)

• Illness with a high fever (Miles Gets Sick and Nobody Notices)

• A relationship between a lecturer and a student that stays strictly non-romantic until she has graduated, and is declared to the department

• Love scenes between the couple after graduation. They are sensual but not explicit (Yu Jie Gets a Job, The Night She Made Him Dance in the Empty Lab)

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
Miles Wei walked into Every Flower in the Shop for one scene, dropped his clicker, asked Elowen if she was happy, and wouldn’t leave my head. This is his book.

I wanted a love story where the most romantic thing anyone does is take the other person’s mind seriously, and where waiting is not a delay but the point. The physics is real, kept at the level of a story: the harmonic oscillator, entropy as counting, strained graphene, and analogue black holes made in water tanks, which real laboratories build.

The jokes are, regrettably, also real. Thank you for reading.
